scenes.heading: Warehouse Query Optimization & Caching
scenes.narration: Fast warehouse queries come from reading less data and reusing prior work through layered caches.

scenes.heading: Levers for faster queries
bullets: Prune aggressively so scans read only relevant partitions.
Filter and aggregate early to shrink data before joins.
Avoid SELECT star so columnar storage skips unused columns.
Read the query profile to find the true bottleneck stage.
scenes.narration: The biggest wins come from pruning and from filtering data down before expensive joins run. Selecting only needed columns lets columnar storage skip the rest entirely. When in doubt, the query profile shows exactly where time and bytes are spent so you optimize the real bottleneck.

scenes.heading: The caching layers
scenes.narration: Snowflake first checks the result cache, which can return an identical query's answer in milliseconds. If that misses, it looks in the warehouse's local disk cache of recently read data. Only when both miss does it read from remote storage, after which the results are cached again.

scenes.heading: Result cache vs data cache

right.title: Local (data) cache
points: Warms up as the warehouse runs

scenes.narration: The result cache serves whole answers when the exact same query runs again on unchanged data. The local data cache instead holds the raw partitions a warehouse has already read, accelerating related queries. This is one reason keeping a warehouse warm can be worth the small idle cost for busy workloads.

scenes.heading: Profiling and pruning a query
scenes.code:
-- Inspect execution details for the last query
SELECT * FROM TABLE(GET_QUERY_OPERATOR_STATS(LAST_QUERY_ID()));

-- Optimized: prune by date, project only needed columns
SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM orders
WHERE order_date >= '2026-07-01'
GROUP BY customer_id;
scenes.narration: The operator stats function reveals how many partitions were scanned versus pruned for the last query. The rewritten query filters on order date so the engine prunes to a narrow range of partitions. It also projects just two columns, so columnar storage skips everything else and the scan stays small.

scenes.text: Optimize by reading less data and reusing caches; the query profile tells you exactly where to focus.
scenes.narration: Read less, cache more, and always let the query profile guide where you spend your tuning effort.
